a dalmatian in the senior chapter is not a generic dog. for this dalmatian, adult weight lands around 45-70 lb (20-32 kg), lifespan is typically 11-13 years, and day-to-day temperament looks like this: high-energy coach dog; water intake and urate stone prevention matter. this dalmatian senior guide focuses on mobility, thirst, appetite trends, and tighter loops around urinary stones (urate). what normal looks like for a senior dalmatian

senior timing for a dalmatian often starts earlier in the large class than in toy companions. for this dalmatian, use mobility, sleep, and thirst, not only birthday candles. pain is not a personality upgrade in an older dalmatian. for this dalmatian, video the gait every ninety days on the same floor. night pacing, potty accidents, and disorientation in a senior dalmatian are cognitive data points, not "just old."

medication logs beat memory once a dalmatian is on more than one daily drug. for this dalmatian, coat care still matters because mats and moisture hide sores: short coat sheds heavily. for this dalmatian, shorten the review interval when urinary stones (urate) or deafness risk is active, and keep lab pdfs beside the weight curve. breed-linked issues to watch in this stage

faqs.question: What is a normal adult weight range for a Dalmatian?
faqs.answer: This breed record lists 45-70 lb (20-32 kg). Your veterinarian sets the target for the individual using body condition, not only the breed average.

faqs.question: Which health issues should I watch for in a senior Dalmatian?
faqs.answer: This stage guide highlights Urinary stones (urate); Deafness risk; Allergies. Use the linked symptom pages for red flags, then contact your clinic.

faqs.question: How often should I weigh my Dalmatian at this stage?
faqs.answer: At least every 30 days for a senior Dalmatian, sooner if appetite, thirst, or mobility changes.
